teaser.text: Enbridge is easiest to understand as a network business: it owns routes, storage and energy facilities, then charges others to use them. A dollar enters through a toll, utility bill, contract or commodity sale, and leaves through suppliers, workers, maintenance, interest, taxes and new investment.

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted forecast is below today’s price in the first two years and only modestly ahead after three years, including dividends. From today’s C$66.51, the weighted value is C$60.54 in October 2027, C$60.66 in October 2028 and C$61.54 in October 2029, producing returns of negative 3%, positive 3% and positive 11%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Enbridge Inc.?

paragraphs.text: That choice reflects adjusted EBITDA rising from C$14,001 million in 2021 to C$19,952 million in 2025, alongside management’s 2026 guidance midpoint of C$20,500 million. Mainline competition, project delays and leverage above the 4.5–5.0 target range justify the bear path, while high utilization, gas demand and projects entering service support the bull case.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Enbridge Inc. really make?

paragraphs.text: Common dividends paid were C$8,220 million. DCF therefore left roughly C$4,234 million before growth spending, while free cash flow after total capital spending was only C$3,051 million. The difference had to come from borrowing, partners, asset sales or equity. Cash distributions from joint ventures can help, but their repeatability must be tested rather than assumed.

dividend.opening: Enbridge’s annualized common dividend is C$3.88 per share for 2026. DCF covers it, but 2025 real free cash flow after total capital spending, leases and stock pay was C$2.766 billion versus C$8.220 billion of dividends.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Enbridge Inc.’s business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Enbridge Inc. pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Enbridge’s preferred dividend measure looks comfortable because DCF deducts maintenance spending, not the entire growth program. The company raised its annualized common dividend to C$3.88 per share for 2026. Against 2025 DCF of C$5.71 per share, that used about 68%, within its target range.

blocks.heading: Is Enbridge Inc.'s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The stricter measure tells a different story. In 2025, real free cash flow after total capital spending, leases and stock pay was C$2.766 billion, while dividends were C$8.220 billion. That left a C$5.454 billion gap. Borrowing can fill it, but creates interest costs; issuing shares can fill it, but dilutes owners.

blocks.heading: What could change Enbridge Inc.'s dividend?

paragraphs.text: The dividend grows at 3% annually in the base case, from C$4.00 in October 2027 to C$4.24 in October 2029. The bear case holds it at C$3.88 because leverage and investment take priority; the bull case reaches C$4.45 because project cash flow grows faster. The base follows the stated increase and the company’s record of annual increases, while the bear reflects the funding pressure.

From 2027 through 2029, leverage staying above target or another equity offering would weaken DCF per share and increase dilution. A higher required return would then compress the multiple by October 2029.

paragraphs.text: The yield is therefore supported by cash, but the next question is how much confidence the market has already placed on that cash.

earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Enbridge Inc.'s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Enbridge Inc. guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: For 2026, Enbridge guides to adjusted EBITDA and DCF per share, while paying an annual dividend of C$3.88. The payout sits within management’s 60–70% range, leaving part of DCF to fund growth.

July reaffirmed the outlook. The Tallgrass acquisition, announced in September, was expected to have no material effect on 2026 guidance because it would close late in the year; its first full year should add to DCF per share. Management also reaffirmed approximately 5.0% growth, but gave no bridge showing how much comes from acquisitions, existing operations or new shares.

blocks.heading: Did Enbridge Inc. keep its past promise?

paragraphs.text: Enbridge forecast 2025 distributable cash flow per share at C$5.50–C$5.90. It reported C$5.71, meeting that promise. Its July 2026 presentation maintained a range of C$5.70–C$6.10 for the next year, but that commitment remains to be tested.

blocks.heading: What has Enbridge Inc.'s revenue and profit trend been?

paragraphs.text: The second quarter of 2026 showed modest operating improvement, while accounting movements made reported earnings look much weaker.

Operating income rose to C$2,910 million, while adjusted EBITDA reached C$4,776 million. DCF increased to C$2,948 million. Net income nevertheless fell because unrealized derivatives, higher depreciation and higher interest absorbed much of the operating improvement.
